comments.note: run_queue.py module docstring uses camelCase field names (e.g. expectedSlug, expectedRepo) matching the JSON output. The new expectedRepo field is documented as nullable to signal legacy-entry detection — this pattern is consistent with how the GUI consumer already handles null checks.

cli.py derives repo_name with a local try/except IndexError block rather than reusing _derive_ledger_log_dir() internals. This is intentional duplication to keep the register() call site self-contained; the pattern mirrors the existing _derive_ledger_log_dir() implementation. A future refactor could extract a _derive_repo_name(plan_dir) helper to DRY both call sites.

The empty-string guard `plan_dir.parents[3].name or None` in cli.py converts an empty string to None, matching the _derive_ledger_log_dir() fallback. This is defensive and correct given that Path.name can return an empty string for root-level paths.

Edge cases: (1) shallow path IndexError guard in cli.py correctly falls back to None; (2) deep path parents[3] correctly resolves repo name; (3) None serializes as JSON null (not omitted); (4) multiple entries in queue each get independent expectedRepo values; (5) unicode/special-char repo names serialize correctly.
Ruff lint: all checks passed on run_queue.py and cli.py.

comments.note: Edge case: passing an empty string '' as repo_name writes expectedRepo: '' in JSON (not null). cli.py guards against this with `or None`, but direct callers of run_queue.register() could pass '' and get an empty-string entry. A guard in register() itself (e.g. `repo_name = repo_name or None`) would make the API more robust, but this is not an AC failure — current behaviour is consistent and testable.

The unregister() cleanup path in cli.py wraps the entire register block in a bare `except Exception` (line 792), which silently swallows any register() failures. This is intentional by design (non-fatal), but means a broken queue file would go undetected. Acceptable for the current scope but worth noting for future monitoring.

summary: Code review PASS with one Fix-Forward applied.

run_queue.py: Parameter addition is clean and idiomatic. Signature, docstring, and module-level shape documentation are all correct and consistent. Entry dict uses camelCase keys matching all existing fields.

cli.py: Derivation pattern (lines 781–784) correctly mirrors _derive_ledger_log_dir() structure. The 'or None' empty-string guard is defensive and correct. Intentional difference from _derive_ledger_log_dir() (None vs 'unknown' fallback) is justified by the null-semantics contract of the queue JSON.

test_run_queue.py: Test coverage is thorough. TestRegisterExpectedRepo class covers all key paths (supplied, omitted, None explicit, slug independence, both keys present). test_entry_shape_is_correct correctly updated to assert expectedRepo: null on default call.

Fix-Forward applied: Added `repo_name = repo_name or None` normalization inside register() to prevent callers from accidentally writing an empty-string expectedRepo. This makes the function's own contract unambiguous without changing behavior for current callers (cli.py already guards at call-site). All 19 run_queue tests pass post-fix.

DRY note (not blocking): _derive_ledger_log_dir() and the register() call-site both use plan_dir.parents[3].name with IndexError fallback, but with different defaults (str vs None). Extracting a _derive_repo_name(plan_dir, fallback=None) helper would be a clean future refactor — deferred as tech debt.

comments.note: run_queue.py register(): Added `repo_name = repo_name or None` at the top of the function body (before entry dict construction). Rationale: QA correctly flagged that passing repo_name='' would write expectedRepo: '' in JSON — an empty string, not null. This violates the documented str | None contract. The one-liner normalises any falsy string to None, making the function self-consistent. Non-behavioral: no existing caller passes an empty string (cli.py guards with 'or None' at call-site). All 19 tests pass post-fix.

Future refactor opportunity: _derive_ledger_log_dir() (line 118–121) and the register() call-site (lines 781–784) both derive plan_dir.parents[3].name with an IndexError guard, but use different fallbacks ('unknown' vs None). A shared helper _derive_repo_name(plan_dir, fallback=None) would DRY both sites. Deferred — current duplication is minor and the implementations are correct.
